rationale: Start with a broad organic window and moderate gradient duration to locate all 10 peaks while limiting late-elution risk. The retention and resolution pattern will identify the useful gradient window and critical pairs for subsequent refinement.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the lone critical pair responds to reduced slope. The current 8.30-minute last peak leaves room to improve separation while likely keeping all peaks within 10 minutes.

Raise temperature by one step while retaining the improved gradient slope to test selectivity of the remaining critical pair. Faster elution should also create time margin for further slope refinement if needed.

The critical pair approached co-elution as temperature rose, suggesting a nearby elution-order reversal. Test 55 C to separate it on the other side of that crossover while shortening retention; the other pairs currently have substantial resolution margins.

Shorten the gradient at 55 C: after the apparent critical-pair order reversal, a steeper slope may now improve its resolution rather than reduce it. This should also shorten the run, while testing whether the neighboring pairs retain adequate separation.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so test a shorter gradient to find the fastest fully resolved method. Monitor the narrow margins around pairs (4,5) and (6,7), retaining injection 5 as the fully resolved benchmark.

Test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to shorten retention while restoring a shallower slope than injection 6. This probes whether trimming the initial gradient window can preserve full resolution, with injection 5 retained as the maximum-score benchmark.

With a maximum-score method secured, test a substantially faster, hotter gradient for a new selectivity window beyond the approaching early-pair crossover. This exploratory run will show whether reordered peaks can regain full resolution at much shorter retention times.

Explore a cooler selectivity branch at the shorter gradient, since the hot, fast method introduced two critical pairs. This tests whether temperature-driven reordering can recover full resolution below the 7.60-minute benchmark.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction separates the reordered early pair at 60 C, while a longer gradient than injection 8 opens the neighboring gap. Injection 5 remains the maximum-score fallback as we search for a faster fully resolved method.

Increase the starting organic fraction to shift selectivity of the sole unresolved pair on the hot, reordered branch. Check that the earlier peaks remain sufficiently retained and separated while seeking full resolution in about five minutes.

Return to the successful 55 C branch and slightly narrow injection 7’s gradient window. The shallower slope should bring its lone unresolved pair toward baseline resolution while potentially matching or slightly shortening injection 5’s last-peak time.

Narrow the gradient window one more step to lift injection 12’s critical pair above 1.5 while retaining adequate separation of the other close pair. This targets another maximum-score method with improved resolution margin and a last peak still comfortably below 10 minutes.

Test a shallower gradient at 60 C to move the early critical pair back onto its resolved, longer-gradient branch. The higher temperature should give the other close pair more separation margin, potentially yielding a robust maximum-score method with all peaks within 10 minutes.

With maximum CRF secured, explore the low-temperature limit and a faster gradient for an alternative elution order. This tests whether the crowded group seen at 30 C separates beyond its temperature crossovers, potentially providing a shorter fully resolved method.

Seek a larger resolution margin around the maximum-score region by combining a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient. This should strengthen the two limiting separations while keeping the first peaks retained and the last peak below 10 minutes.

Reduce the endpoint by one grid step to improve injection 16’s lone unresolved pair through a shallower slope. Its 1.74 resolution margin at the other critical pair and 8.54-minute last peak leave room to seek full resolution without a time penalty.

With maximum CRF secured, test a rapid gradient followed by a moderate-organic hold as an alternative route to a shorter separation. The hold may spread later peaks differently from the continuous gradients; monitor both the crowded middle group and last-peak retention.

Refine the fully resolved injection 17 with one step shallower slope to increase its limiting resolution margin. The estimated last peak is just below 10 minutes, so this tests the boundary for a more robust maximum-score method.

Trim injection 5’s unused high-organic tail while preserving its starting fraction, temperature, and exact gradient slope. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends, preserving maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test a gradient slope between the fully resolved injection 5 and the faster but unresolved injection 6. This finer slope adjustment targets a shorter last-peak time while checking whether the early critical pair remains above R = 1.5.

Preserve the proven gradient slope through all critical pairs, then elute the isolated final compound during the hold. This tests a lower-organic endpoint and shorter programmed gradient while aiming to retain full resolution and a last peak below 10 minutes.

Refine the fully resolved injection 13 by one endpoint step to improve its early critical-pair margin while checking the other close pair. This targets a maximum-score alternative with more balanced resolution margins and ample time below the 10-minute cutoff.

Test a slope between injections 12 and 13 to approach the shortest fully resolved method at this starting fraction. The critical pair is predicted to remain just above R = 1.5, with the last peak around 7.8 minutes and no time penalty.

Test a slightly shallower slope near the fastest maximum-score method to improve the early critical pair while checking that the other close pair stays above R = 1.5. Injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved benchmark, with CRF 1.000 and a 7.60-minute last peak.
